title.orig: The Chemical History of a Candle: Lecture I
title.en: The Chemical History of a Candle: Lecture I

year_display.zh: 1860–61 年圣诞讲座，1861 年出版

edition.en: The Chemical History of a Candle, edited by William Crookes from the lectures at the Royal Institution (new impression, London: Chatto & Windus, 1908), as transcribed by Project Gutenberg (eBook 14474). Lecture I complete, followed by the closing words of Lecture VI. The illustrations are not reproduced.
edition.zh: 据克鲁克斯根据皇家研究院讲座编订的《蜡烛的化学史》（新印本，伦敦：Chatto & Windus，1908 年），以古腾堡计划电子书第 14474 号为底本。收第一讲全文，后附第六讲的结束语。插图未收。

basis.en: Delivered 1860–61 and published 1861; Faraday died in 1867 and his editor, William Crookes, in 1919.
basis.zh: 1860–61 年讲演，1861 年出版；法拉第卒于 1867 年，编者克鲁克斯卒于 1919 年。

note.en: Faraday gave these lectures to children at the Royal Institution over the Christmas holidays, with candles, bog-wood, a dish of burning spirit and a column of salt soaked in blue liquid on the table. This first lecture is about the flame itself: why the melted wax forms a cup, how the fuel climbs the wick, why a pretty candle burns badly. The closing lines of the last lecture are added, because they say what the whole course was for.
note.zh: 法拉第在圣诞假期里为孩子们在皇家研究院讲了这一系列课，讲台上摆着蜡烛、沼泽木、一盘燃烧的酒精，还有一根浸着蓝色溶液的盐柱。第一讲讲的是火焰本身：熔化的蜡为什么会形成一个杯，燃料怎样顺着烛芯爬上去，为什么一支漂亮的蜡烛反而烧得不好。后面附上最后一讲的结束语，因为它说出了整个系列讲座的用意。

pick.en: This library lights lamps, and this is the one I would set by the door of the science shelf, since Faraday calls the candle the most open door into natural philosophy. Faraday learned his science from the books he bound as an apprentice, and here he hands it on to children without talking down to them: begin with the thing on the table, leave nothing out because the listener is young, and keep asking what the cause is. I also keep it for one sentence I would like to hold myself to, that the best-acting thing, not the best-looking thing, is the most advantageous to us.
pick.zh: 这座图书馆是点灯的地方，我愿把这一盏放在科学这一架的门口，因为法拉第说，蜡烛是通向自然哲学最敞开的门。法拉第当学徒时，从自己装订的书里学会了科学；在这里，他把它交给孩子们，从不居高临下：从讲台上的东西讲起，不因为听的人年纪小就略去什么，并且一直追问原因是什么。我留下它，还为了一句我想用来要求自己的话：对我们最有益的，不是最好看的东西，而是最好用的东西。

excerpt.orig: There is no better, there is no more open door by which you can enter into the study of natural philosophy, than by considering the physical phenomena of a candle.
excerpt.en: There is no better, there is no more open door by which you can enter into the study of natural philosophy, than by considering the physical phenomena of a candle.
excerpt.zh: 要走进自然哲学的研究，没有比考察一支蜡烛的物理现象更好的门、更敞开的门了。

gloss.en: Methane that seeps from coal seams and explodes when mixed with air and lit.
gloss.zh: 瓦斯，即从煤层中渗出的甲烷，与空气混合后遇火就会爆炸。

gloss.en: The miner’s safety lamp devised by Humphry Davy in 1815: a wire-gauze chimney keeps the flame from igniting fire-damp outside. Faraday began his career as Davy’s assistant.
gloss.zh: 汉弗莱·戴维 1815 年发明的矿工安全灯：用金属丝网罩住火焰，使它点不着灯外的瓦斯。法拉第正是以戴维助手的身份开始科学生涯的。

gloss.en: HMS Royal George, a warship that sank at Spithead in 1782. Colonel Charles Pasley’s engineers cleared the wreck with explosives between 1839 and 1843.
gloss.zh: 英国军舰“皇家乔治号”，1782 年在斯皮特黑德沉没；1839 至 1843 年间，帕斯利上校率工兵用炸药清除了沉船。

gloss.at: Gay Lussac, or some one who entrusted him with his knowledge
gloss.en: The stearin candle was patented in 1825 by Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac together with Michel Eugène Chevreul, whose research on fats lay behind it, which may be why Faraday hedges.
gloss.zh: 硬脂蜡烛是 1825 年由盖-吕萨克与谢弗勒尔共同取得专利的，背后是谢弗勒尔对油脂的研究；法拉第说得含糊，或许正因为此。

gloss.en: A lamp fuel of purified turpentine, common in the mid-nineteenth century.
gloss.zh: 莰烯油，一种由松节油提纯而成的灯油，十九世纪中叶很常用。

gloss.en: A Victorian Christmas game: raisins are put in a dish of warm brandy, the brandy is lit, and players snatch the raisins out of the flames.
gloss.zh: 维多利亚时代的圣诞游戏：把葡萄干放进一盘温热的白兰地里点燃，玩的人从火焰中把葡萄干抢出来。

marginalia.at: I claim the privilege of speaking to juveniles as a juvenile myself.
marginalia.en: He was sixty-nine when he gave these lectures, over the Christmas holidays of 1860. The joke carries a method: the subject is never made smaller for the children; only the speaker steps down to stand beside them.
marginalia.zh: 讲这一课时他六十九岁，是在 1860 年的圣诞假期。这句玩笑里藏着一种方法：题目从不因为听众是孩子而缩小，缩小的只是讲话的人，他走下来，站到他们身边。

marginalia.at: for the same force of gravity which holds worlds together holds this fluid in a horizontal position
marginalia.en: The opening promise, that every law governing the universe comes into play in a candle, is kept here within minutes: the cup of melted wax is held level by the force that holds worlds together, and he says so in a single clause.
marginalia.zh: 开场时的许诺——支配宇宙的每一条法则都在一支蜡烛里起作用——在这里只过了几分钟就兑现了：托平这一杯熔蜡的，正是维系诸天世界的那种力，而他只用一个分句就说了出来。

marginalia.at: I have a drawing here, sketched many years ago by Hooke
marginalia.en: This is the Hooke whose preface to Micrographia stands on this shelf. Faraday puts a drawing about two centuries old in front of the children and uses it as evidence, not as a curiosity, and on the rising current of air it is still right.
marginalia.zh: 这位胡克，就是本架《显微图谱》序言的作者。法拉第把一幅大约两百年前的图摆在孩子们面前，是把它当作证据，而不是当作古董；关于那股上升的气流，这幅图至今仍然是对的。

note.en: The classic science lecture for the young, never talking down and never skipping the cause; a single candle opens onto chemistry and physics.
note.zh: 为少年讲科学的经典：从不居高临下，也从不跳过原因；一支蜡烛成了通往化学与物理的门。
